verses.text: The LORD said to Moses,
"This is the teaching for a person with a serious skin disease on the day he is made clean. He must be brought to the priest,
and the priest will go outside the camp to look at him. If the person has been healed of the disease,
the priest will order that two live clean birds be brought for him, with cedar wood, red yarn, and a hyssop branch.
The priest will order that one bird be killed over fresh running water in a clay pot.
Then he will take the live bird, the cedar wood, the red yarn, and the hyssop, and dip them with the live bird in the blood of the bird killed over the running water.
He will sprinkle the blood seven times on the person being made clean of the skin disease, and say he is clean. Then he will let the live bird fly away into the open fields.

The person being made clean must wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe in water. Then he will be clean. After that he may come into the camp, but he must stay outside his tent for seven days.
On the seventh day he must shave off all his hair: his head, his beard, his eyebrows, and all the rest. He must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and then he will be clean.

On the eighth day he must bring two male lambs and one one-year-old female lamb, all with nothing wrong with them, about four and a half kilograms of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and about a third of a litre of oil.
The priest who makes him clean will place the man and these offerings in front of the LORD at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
The priest will take one of the male lambs and offer it as a guilt offering, with the oil. He will wave them in front of the LORD as a wave offering.
He will kill the lamb in the holy area, where the sin offering and the burnt offering are killed. Like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest. It is most holy.

The priest will take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the bottom of the right ear of the person being made clean, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
Then the priest will pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand.
He will dip a finger of his right hand into the oil in his left hand, and sprinkle some of it with his finger seven times in front of the LORD.

The priest will put some of the oil left in his hand on the bottom of the person's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
He will put the rest of the oil in his hand on the head of the person being made clean. In this way the priest will make him right with God in front of the LORD.
Then the priest will offer the sin offering to make the person right with God for his uncleanness. After that he will kill the burnt offering.
The priest will offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. In this way the priest will make him right with God, and he will be clean.

But if the person is poor and cannot afford all this, he may bring one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved, to make him right with God, with about one and a half kilograms of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and about a third of a litre of oil.
He must also bring two doves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
On the eighth day he must bring them to the priest at the door of the Tent of Meeting, in front of the LORD, to be made clean.
The priest will take the lamb for the guilt offering and the oil, and wave them in front of the LORD as a wave offering.

He will kill the lamb for the guilt offering. Then he will take some of its blood and put it on the bottom of the right ear of the person being made clean, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest will pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand.
With a finger of his right hand, he will sprinkle some of the oil from his left hand seven times in front of the LORD.

He will put some of the oil in his hand on the bottom of the person's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, in the same places as the blood of the guilt offering.
He will put the rest of the oil in his hand on the head of the person being made clean, to make him right with God in front of the LORD.
Then he will offer the doves or the young pigeons, whichever the person can afford,
one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. In this way the priest will make the person right with God in front of the LORD."
This is the teaching for someone with a serious skin disease who cannot afford the usual offerings for being made clean.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"When you come into the land of Canaan, which I am giving you to own, I may put spreading mould in a house in that land.
Then the owner of the house must go and tell the priest, 'I think I see something like mould in my house.'
Before the priest goes in to look at the mould, he must order that the house be emptied, so that nothing in it will become unclean. Then the priest will go in to look at the house.
He will look at the mould. If it is on the walls in sunken greenish or reddish patches that seem deeper than the surface of the wall,
the priest will go out to the door of the house and close it up for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest will come back and look. If the mould has spread on the walls,
the priest will order that the stones with the mould be pulled out and thrown into an unclean place outside the town.
He will have the inside walls of the house scraped all over, and the plaster that is scraped off must be dumped in an unclean place outside the town.
Then they must take other stones to replace the old ones, and use new plaster to cover the house.
If the mould comes back and breaks out in the house after the stones have been pulled out and the house scraped and plastered,
the priest will come and look. If the mould has spread in the house, it is a harmful mould, and the house is unclean.
It must be torn down, its stones, its wood, and all its plaster, and carried out of the town to an unclean place.
Anyone who goes into the house while it is closed up will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sleeps or eats in the house must wash his clothes.
But if the priest comes and looks, and the mould has not spread after the house was plastered, he will say the house is clean, because the mould is gone.
To make the house clean, he must take two birds, cedar wood, red yarn, and hyssop.
He will kill one bird over fresh running water in a clay pot.
Then he will take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the red yarn, and the live bird, dip them in the blood of the dead bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
He will make the house clean with the bird's blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the red yarn.
Then he will let the live bird fly away out of the town into the open fields. In this way he will make the house right, and it will be clean."
This is the teaching for every kind of serious skin disease and itching sore,
for mould on clothing or in a house,
and for a swelling, a scab, or a shiny spot.
It teaches when something is unclean and when it is clean. This is the teaching about serious skin diseases and mould.
